saintfeast.title: Cosmas and Damianos the Holy Unmercenaries and their mother Theodota

lectionaryreading.title: St. Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians 12:27-31; 13:1-8

translation.title: Reading
translation.body: These Saints were from Asia (that is, Asia Minor). After the death of their father, their Christ-loving mother Theodota reared them in piety and in all manner of virtue, and had them instructed in every science, especially that of medicine. This became their vocation, and they went about healing every illness and malady, bestowing healing freely on both men and beasts alike; because of this, they are called "Unmercenaries." And thus, having completed the course of their life, they reposed in peace.

hymn.title: Apolytikion of Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian in the Third Tone
hymn.shorttitle: Apolytikion of Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian

translation.body: Sainted Unmercenaries and Wonder Workers, regard our infirmities; freely you have received, freely share with us.

hymn.title: Kontakion of Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian in the Second Tone
hymn.shorttitle: Kontakion of Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian

translation.body: O glorious, wonderworking physicians, having received the grace of healing, you reach out and restore health to those in need. But also, by your visitation you cast down the arrogance of the enemy, healing the world through miracles.
